patch_description: The current algorithm routes every partition of every destination along a single Dijkstra shortest path. This (1) concentrates all traffic on one path, causing congestion/throughput bottlenecks, and (2) ignores parallel low-cost alternatives across multi-cloud networks. Improvement: for each (src, dst) pair, compute k shortest simple paths using `nx.shortest_simple_paths` (ranked by cumulative cost), then distribute the `num_partitions` across these paths using a greedy least-loaded assignment. This balances load across networks, exploits parallel links, and lowers effective transfer cost by avoiding saturated high-throughput edges. Since partition paths may share edges with other destinations, we also track per-edge assigned partition counts and prefer paths minimizing (path_cost / available_paths) weighted by current edge load, reducing redundant heavy usage of the same links.
